about: The capability vocabulary a plan variant may `require` or `lacks`, each capability's class, the coarse-chunk threshold and a last chunk's assumed fill. Read by C++ (compiled in) and Python (kvevaluator.contract); the fields, and why each format's capability RULES are code and not here: cpp/kvevaluator/src/contract/README.md.
chunk_coarse_doc: The pack target (bytes, Format.pack_target) from which a store holds coarse_chunks: the paper's c512k arm. One threshold, so a third arm (c4k, c1048576k) falls on one side of it; a valued cap would change the IR selector contract on both sides. Changing it changes which body a chunked store selects: bump the C++ counting versions with it (formats/registry.cc kFormatCounting).
last_chunk_fill_doc: The share of its pack target a Chunked family's last chunk is taken to hold where its true fill is not used: the half chunk view charges a write's last-chunk touch target x this (kvcost.layout_cost.compose.chunk_view), and a sampled tally, which reads only its sample, writes a sampled family's last_chunk_value_bytes as target x this (kvevaluator tally). Half: a last chunk is anywhere from empty to full, depending on where earlier chunk edges fell, not on the layout.
class_doc: validity: a body that relies on it returns WRONG rows, or fails, on a format without it, so a measured choice among a bundle's bodies may never pick a body whose validity caps the format lacks. selector: it only picks the cheaper body; every body that names it still answers correctly without it. Evidence: each body of every bundle forced on formats lacking its caps (sf0.1 Python store, 348 runs), plus the op code cited per cap.

sorted_range_index.doc: a value-sorted index a range walk can stop early on
sorted_range_index.evidence: read_index_range on a day-granular index returns the boundary days' superset and ignores labels (formats/dgraph.py read_index_range); the sorted body has no exact re-check: entry_range DIFFERENT

value_sorted_index.doc: the index posting's ENTRIES are ordered by the sort value (dgraph dim-2: a day-token posting stored date-descending), so a ranked top-k reads each bucket's value already in order and ranks with no per-candidate value GET. Nebula and arangodb get it free (value in the key). A strict add-on to sorted_range_index
value_sorted_index.evidence: no body names it; the formats branch on their own schema, not on the cap

key_sorted_index.doc: the index puts the sort value IN THE KEY, one entry per value (dgraph dim-2 option B: an ms+vid composite token per message), so a ranked top-k key range scan reads exactly K key-only entries and stops. A strict add-on to sorted_range_index, advertised so a future plan can demand the byte-optimal walk
key_sorted_index.evidence: is2's body ranks in memory from props read per candidate, no index walk: 5/5 SAME

unsorted_range_index.doc: a whole-posting index that must be read then re-filtered
unsorted_range_index.evidence: the bucket walk (index_range_buckets) exists on dgraph only: AttributeError elsewhere

date_keyed_adjacency.doc: adjacency ordered by a date property (a per-source window walk)
date_keyed_adjacency.evidence: the dated adjacency walks: no format implements them (no format keeps its adjacency sorted by date)

per_type_index.doc: the index is scoped per vertex or edge type (the index IS the type filter)
per_type_index.evidence: dgraph's shared index: index_range_buckets ignores labels, so entry_range's candidate-free body counts other types' dates (DIFFERENT); top-k raises without candidates

label_scoped_props.doc: a vertex's props are keyed under its label: a props read under another label misses (reads nulls), the fused twins' filter test (dgraph's keys are label-free)
label_scoped_props.evidence: the fused filter (plans/ir/lowering.py) tests a non-null prop read under the label; dgraph's props are label-free: ic4's fused body 10 rows vs 3

whole_row_read.doc: a vertex read returns the entire row or document at once (a row or blob store), so a rank read already carries the body and one-phase wins; dgraph splits properties across keys and needs two-phase
whole_row_read.evidence: one-phase bodies read the same props per vertex on a split store: 45/45 SAME

type_index.doc: a type index of ANY kind: the type filter can enter by the index (read_filter_by_label_index), 1 SEEK on a single posting, a whole-type scan on a per-vertex index. Held by dgraph when the design declares the type index, and by every per-type-index format. Selected by filter_by_label(via="index"); a variant `on` a label checks that label's caps
type_index.evidence: read_filter_by_label_index enumerates the type; dgraph without the declared type index raises, only when candidates are non-empty (data-dependent)

type_index_single_posting.doc: the whole type's membership is ONE value, so entering by the type index costs 1 SEEK whatever the type size (dgraph's dgraph.type posting; arango's collection-qualified id is free either way). A per-vertex type index (nebula, pertype_csr) is not this. Selects read_filter_by_label_index over the per-candidate probe
type_index_single_posting.evidence: its bodies use read_filter_by_label_index, right on any type index (a whole-type scan where not single-posting): 12/12 SAME; they need type_index (9/9 ERROR on dgraph@no_type_index)

index_entries_by_docid.doc: the index's entries identify an INTERNAL docid, not the vid (arango's persistent index: docid in the key, the _key in the document), so a candidate-filtered index walk pays a document GET per crossed entry, which makes a one-phase whole-row read cheaper there than the walk. The property behind the ic8 one_phase pick

label_scan_carries_props.doc: a type enumeration walks the structure that HOLDS the rows, so a label scan can project properties in the same pass (read_vertices_by_label(props=...)): the chunked per-type layout. A vid-only type index (nebula's tag index, dgraph's type posting) enumerates ids and needs a read per vertex. Selects the fused scan over enumerate + re-read
label_scan_carries_props.evidence: read_vertices_by_label(props=...) exists on pertype_csr and meta, per label; TypeError elsewhere. This cap marks meta's Chunked labels, label_rows_one_run all of them

label_rows_one_run.doc: per label: the label's records are one contiguous key run, so one sequential scan of the run may read the label with its props (read_vertices_by_label(props=..., keep=...)): 1 SEEK + 1 NEXT per key of the run. Validity only; the pick decides whether the scan is cheaper. Held by pertype_csr, every props layout of meta and arangodb
label_rows_one_run.evidence: read_vertices_by_label with props (and keep) runs where the label's records are one key run: pertype_csr, meta (per label) and arangodb; dgraph and nebula refuse props

whole_label_scan_by_default.doc: per label: a whole-label read with props runs as that one scan by default, the selector of the fused-scan bodies of the microbench whole-label scans (entry_eq_scan, entry_range_scan, topk10_scan). Held where label_rows_one_run is, except arangodb: its scan is built and valid, the default is held until the other formats' whole-label scans are sized
whole_label_scan_by_default.evidence: the fused scan answers wherever the label's rows are one run: forced on arangodb 9/9 SAME (sf0.1 Python store)

coarse_chunks.doc: a STORE property, not a format's: the store packs rows into chunks of >= chunk_coarse bytes, so one landing on a row decodes a big chunk. Derived from the format's pack target (pertype_csr's chunk target, meta's smallest vertex-props pack; dgraph's chunk target is a split threshold, not a pack), never declared by a format
coarse_chunks.evidence: both bodies answer on every chunk arm; it only picks: ic3's full_read beats the dated-index walk on pertype_csr-c512k (1.218x at sf30, pin check) while the walk wins at c64k

property_index.doc: a STORE property, not a format's: the schema declares property indexes (value or date), so a body that reads one (the ops whose `requires` names it in kv_ops.json) has its index. Derived from the schema, never declared by a format. Stamped by the plan dumper from a body's ops at emit, never inherited from a pick's rules
property_index.evidence: an index read on a design that declares no property index: nebula, arangodb, pertype_csr and meta throw; dgraph reads an index never written and returns no rows (entry_eq 0 vs 5, topk10 0 vs 10 on dgraph-label_only sf0.1)

reverse_adjacency.doc: per EDGE TYPE (an `on` that names the edge type): the store keeps this edge type's in lists, so a read_edge_exists read with dir "in" is valid. nebula, arangodb, pertype_csr: every edge type; dgraph: the @reverse ones; meta: direction both, or the schema's @reverse
reverse_adjacency.evidence: a read_edge_exists read with dir "in" on an edge type whose in lists are not kept: dgraph and meta raise

adjacency_lists.doc: per EDGE TYPE: its adjacency is a list per owner in EVERY stored direction, with no per-edge key to point-GET (dgraph, arangodb, pertype_csr; meta's Condensed and Chunked). Picks the default reads of a read_edge_exists. Conservative for a store whose directions differ (meta adjacency_by_etype_dir)
adjacency_lists.evidence: both bodies answer on any store that keeps the in lists; the per-edge-key body is the cheaper one there
